description: SMART configuration must be discoverable at .well-known/smart-configuration
remediation_hint: Ensure your FHIR server exposes .well-known/smart-configuration with a valid JSON body.

description: Server must support PKCE S256 code challenge method
Access token must include all requested scopes (patient/*.read minimum)
remediation_hint: Ensure authorization server grants at minimum patient/*.read scope.

description: Server must advertise launch-ehr and launch-standalone capabilities
remediation_hint: Add launch-ehr and launch-standalone to capabilities array in .well-known/smart-configuration.

description: Token response must include patient context and openid/fhirUser claims
remediation_hint: Verify your app requests openid fhirUser scopes and that the token response includes a patient field.

source: SMART App Launch IG v2.0 §4.1.1 (state); OAuth 2.0 Security BCP §4.7
description: App must send an unguessable state and reject a callback whose state does not match
remediation_hint: Generate a random state per launch, store it against the session, and compare it (constant-time) on callback before exchanging the code.

source: RFC 7636 §4.6; SMART App Launch IG v2.0 §7.1
description: Authorization server must reject a token exchange presenting an incorrect PKCE code_verifier
remediation_hint: Advertising S256 is not enough — confirm the server actually verifies it. A server that accepts any verifier offers no protection against code interception.

description: Authorization code must be single-use: replaying a spent code must be refused
remediation_hint: Confirm the server invalidates the code on first exchange. If a replay succeeds, a leaked code stays exploitable.

source: ONC (g)(10) §170.315(g)(10)(v)(A); SMART App Launch IG v2.0 §9.2
description: Patient-scoped token must be refused when reading a different patient's record
remediation_hint: Attempt a read of a patient id other than the one in the token's patient context; the server must return 401/403. Success here is a PHI breach.

source: OpenID Connect Core 1.0 §3.1.3.7; SMART App Launch IG v2.0 §6
description: id_token signature must be verifiable against the issuer's advertised jwks_uri
remediation_hint: Fetch jwks_uri, verify the id_token signature, issuer and audience. An unverified id_token can be forged, so fhirUser identity cannot be trusted.
